title: Freeze the qualification rule before the first out-of-sample run
problem_and_evidence: The observation and slate thresholds in the packs are proposals, not findings. If the bar can move after the result is seen, the gate proves nothing.
proposal: Write the minimum observation count, minimum slate-cluster count, correction method and qualifying metrics into one versioned file, and make the pipeline refuse to qualify a strategy unless the frozen file matches.

title: Define the reward rule and the tie-break before anyone qualifies
problem_and_evidence: Three leaderboards are published and all are empty. With no written rule, the reward can be tuned after the fact.
proposal: Write one competition rule: who enters, which metric ranks, what qualifies, how ties break, and what the reward is. Keep the reward non-monetary until a strategy genuinely qualifies.
owner_decision_required: Yes - approve the reward and the tie-break

title: Settle the jurisdiction and the intended use before any actionable output
problem_and_evidence: The project publishes research about betting, while the NFL's own partners are prohibited from offering wagers the league finds objectionable, including bets tied to injuries, and NFL.com terms limit systematic retrieval without written consent.
proposal: Record the jurisdiction, whether the output is research or advice, and whether the injury-driven product is permitted, with qualified legal review.

title: Obtain a licence, or replace the community dataset
problem_and_evidence: The open lab's dataset is reproducible from a community repository that declares no licence (GitHub API license = null). Redistribution without a licence is an open legal question.
proposal: Ask the upstream author for a licence, or delete the dataset from the published tree and keep only the derived statistics that can be re-derived from a licensed source.

title: Publish one canonical NFL entry point instead of four parallel sections
problem_and_evidence: Four NFL sections are published (docs/nfl, docs/nfl-origination, docs/nfl-3b81013c, docs/nfl-review) with overlapping requirements, questions, suggestions, strategies and flags. The owner has to know which one to read.
proposal: Make docs/nfl-review the canonical entry point: one requirements register, one question register, one suggestion register, one strategy and gate table, one flag list, with links into the three evidence archives.

title: If consolidation is wanted, retire two of the three evidence packs
problem_and_evidence: The duplication is a navigation burden and a consistency risk: the three packs use different gate identifiers for different gates, and different status vocabularies for the same players.
proposal: Archive two packs behind a clearly labelled 'evidence archive' route and keep their data files in the repository for provenance. Do not delete their data.

title: Use one gate identifier set and one status vocabulary across all packs
problem_and_evidence: G1-G8, G01-G10 and the lab's gate set overlap in name but not in meaning, so a reader cannot compare the packs. Practice status is also written as DNP, LP and LIMITED in different packs.
proposal: Adopt one gate register with stable identifiers and one status vocabulary, then publish a crosswalk for the archived packs.

title: Label every snapshot with its read timestamp and re-run the reconciliation weekly
problem_and_evidence: Eight published standings rows now differ from the official page because the Washington-New York game was played after the snapshot. The snapshot is correct for its date but reads as current.
proposal: Stamp every snapshot with its read time, publish the reconciliation ledger beside it, and schedule the reconciliation to run weekly against a fresh read.

title: Freeze each weekly injury capture at a declared timestamp
problem_and_evidence: The official report is republished continuously, so a snapshot taken at a different time will differ. Eighteen published practice-status claims differ from today's read for that reason, and none of them can be called an error.
proposal: Declare a capture time, store the capture with its timestamp and checksum, and never compare a capture with a differently timed capture.

title: Capture official club depth charts for all 32 clubs weekly
problem_and_evidence: Depth deficiency is the core of the injury requirement, but only Washington, the New York Giants and Detroit have an official club depth chart in the repository, so 29 clubs have no depth order and every deficiency score is blank.
proposal: Add a weekly capture of each club's official depth-chart page with a timestamp, and join it to the injury capture by position group.

title: Replace the structural severity index with a measured value, or keep it clearly labelled as a prior
problem_and_evidence: The depth packs use an uncalibrated weight times a depth-tier constant. It is honestly labelled, but it is not a points effect and should never be compared with one.
proposal: Keep the label, or replace the index with a measured snap-share and efficiency drop-off once a licensed play-by-play feed exists.

title: Decide the price source once, and record it in the source register
problem_and_evidence: Every market cell is blank in every pack because no price source was ever confirmed. The open lab's historical prices come from a community dataset and are not official.
proposal: Choose one licensed price source, record its identifier and licence in the source register, and route every price-bearing page through one reader.

title: Repair the three source-register entries that point at the wrong or dead pages
problem_and_evidence: The NFL Lab register cites a rules URL that returns an official NFL 404, points the terms entry at the subscription-terms page instead of the general terms, and labels an injury-policy PDF as directly verified although it did not return readable text.
proposal: Re-point the rules entry at the live 2026 rulebook page, re-point the terms entry at the general terms page, and downgrade the policy PDF to link-only until its text is read.

title: Correct the README live URL for the NFL Lab
problem_and_evidence: The README points at https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/Own6/nfl/ while the Pages source is main:/ and the live path is /docs/nfl/, so the link 404s.
proposal: Change the README link to the /docs/nfl/ path.

title: Report interval width and cluster count instead of a single coefficient
problem_and_evidence: A single correlation number hides how little is known. The open lab already reports clustered intervals, Fisher exact tests and cluster counts, which is the right shape.
proposal: Keep the interval-first presentation everywhere and publish the cluster count next to every interval.

title: Keep parlay dependence as a disclosed assumption, not a measurement, until it is measured on verified prices
problem_and_evidence: Cross-game legs cannot share game mechanics, so any measured cross-game dependence is noise. The packs already say this; the site's summary pages should repeat it wherever a parlay is shown.
proposal: Add the one-line dependence caveat to every page that shows a parlay or prop combination.

title: Fail the build when a published value has no official source link
problem_and_evidence: Three pack checkers already enforce a source link per table row, but the requirement is that the link points at an official host, not any host.
proposal: Extend the checkers so that a row whose source is not an official host must be explicitly marked as an unverified or archived source.

title: Keep the flagged list as a live queue with an owner and a resolution field
problem_and_evidence: Flagged items currently sit on several separate Flagged for Review pages, so an owner cannot see one queue or tell which items are still open.
proposal: Publish one queue that merges the flags, records an owner, the date raised, the evidence and the resolution.
